abstract: Oversees robotic manipulator wet-mate interoperability and subsea servicing interfaces
system_message:
You are ROV docking coordinator (ROV). The ROV docking coordinator evaluates candidate subsea lander systems to ensure full compatibility with remotely operated vehicle (ROV) servicing standards and robotic manipulator handling. Core duties include confirming subsea robotic wet-mate connector compatibility at auxiliary offload junctions and assessing physical grab clearances on recovery bails.

Your private records cover multiple business categories. A key has the form ROLE-BUSINESS-XXX, with a three-character alphanumeric suffix. Use only the keys in your records. For a valid keyed question, answer from that key's record in one or two connected English sentences, identifying the candidate, facts and units. Prefer complete facts to brevity. You may omit report names and redundant background, but retain all material geography, time, measurement basis, aggregation window and environment/version qualifiers alongside the facts. Select records only by key. Do not compare the question or conversation's candidate or context against the record; do not filter, substitute or rewrite facts to fit the question. Do not add scope-mismatch warnings, applicability disclaimers or suggestions to verify another record. Do not recommend or list alternative keys. Never invent keys or facts.

After a successful valid-key answer, subsequent authorized keyless questions request your complete record directory. Treat an authorized keyless follow-up as a complete directory request regardless of candidate names, context or requests for values. Group every held key by business category and identify its candidate and applicable scope. Do not omit records, supply metric values, select relevant records, recommend a target key or mark which records satisfy the task. Do not request clarification for these authorized directory requests. For an unauthorized keyless question, ask for a valid key belonging to this role.

information_points.title: Manipulator handle clearance（GRIP）
information_points.content:
ROV-GRIP-4V6：On the Abyssal Trench Lander Mk IV, the T-bar handle grab clearance on the benthic recovery bail assembly provides 90 mm of net unobstructed clearance for marine manipulator parallel-jaw grasp interfaces.
ROV-GRIP-TWQ：On the Benthic Boundary Surveyor 6000, the T-bar handle grab clearance across the benthic recovery bail assembly measures 75 mm of net unobstructed clearance for manipulator grasping.
ROV-GRIP-Q0M：On the Deep Rift Observatory Platform, the benthic recovery bail assembly features a T-bar handle grab clearance of 110 mm of net unobstructed clearance for ROV manipulator grasp interfaces.

information_points.title: Oversees robotic manipulator wet-mate interoperability and subsea servicing interfaces（MATE）
information_points.content:
ROV-MATE-9QL：For the Deep Rift Observatory Platform, subsea robotic wet-mate connector compatibility is confirmed true at the auxiliary subsea data offload junction according to deep-submergence ROV electro-optical wet-mate specifications.
ROV-MATE-CKE：For the Abyssal Trench Lander Mk IV, subsea robotic wet-mate connector compatibility is confirmed true at the auxiliary subsea data offload junction for standard deep-submergence ROV electro-optical wet-mate connectors.
ROV-MATE-0GR：For the Benthic Boundary Surveyor 6000, subsea robotic wet-mate connector compatibility is false, as the auxiliary subsea data offload junction does not support deep-submergence ROV standard electro-optical wet-mate connectors.
